items.question: Is the image converter free to use?
items.answer: Yes—every converter on imageconverter.dev is free, unlimited, and watermark-free. Convert as many files as you want without creating an account.

items.question: Do my images ever upload to a server?
items.answer: No. All conversions happen entirely in your browser using Web APIs. After the page loads you can even go offline and the converter will keep working.

items.question: Will the converter reduce image quality?
items.answer: We preserve the image resolution and apply gentle compression only when the target format requires it. Transparent backgrounds are automatically flattened to white when exporting to JPG.

items.question: Can I convert multiple images at once?
items.answer: Right now this tool handles one file at a time so you can review the output before downloading. Need bulk conversions? Try our bulk resize tool with format switching support.

png.title: What is PNG?
png.description: PNG (Portable Network Graphics) is a raster graphics file format that supports lossless data compression. It was developed as an improved, non-patented replacement for Graphics Interchange Format (GIF).
png.bestFor: Web graphics, logos, charts, and illustrations requiring transparency.

jpg.title: What is JPG?
jpg.description: JPG (Joint Photographic Experts Group) is a widely used compressed image format for containing digital photographs and other raster graphics. It uses lossy compression to balance image quality and file size.
jpg.bestFor: Photographs, complex images with many colors, and web images where small file size is critical.

webp.title: What is WebP?
webp.description: WebP is a modern image format employed by Google that provides superior lossless and lossy compression for images on the web. It allows webmasters and web developers to create smaller, richer images that make the web faster.
webp.bestFor: Web images (replacing both PNG and JPG) to improve page load speeds.

heic.title: What is HEIC?
heic.description: HEIC (High Efficiency Image Container) is the file format used by Apple for photos on iOS devices. It uses the HEVC (High Efficiency Video Coding) standard to save images with high quality at smaller file sizes than JPG.
heic.bestFor: Storing high-quality photos on mobile devices with limited storage.
pros: High quality at half the size of JPG
Supports Live Photos and depth maps

avif.title: What is AVIF?
avif.description: AVIF (AV1 Image File Format) is an open, royalty-free image file format specification for storing images or image sequences compressed with AV1 in the HEIF file format.
avif.bestFor: Next-generation web images requiring maximum compression efficiency.
pros: HDR and Wide Color Gamut support

svg.title: What is SVG?
svg.description: SVG (Scalable Vector Graphics) is an XML-based vector image format for two-dimensional graphics with support for interactivity and animation. Unlike raster images, SVGs can be scaled infinitely without losing quality.
svg.bestFor: Logos, icons, and simple illustrations that need to look sharp at any size.
pros: Tiny file size for simple graphics

tiff.title: What is TIFF?
tiff.description: TIFF (Tagged Image File Format) is a computer file format for storing raster graphics images, popular among graphic artists, the publishing industry, and photographers.
tiff.bestFor: Professional photography, printing, and scanning where quality is paramount.

gif.title: What is GIF?
gif.description: GIF (Graphics Interchange Format) is a bitmap image format that supports animations. It uses LZW lossless data compression and allows up to 256 colors per frame.
gif.bestFor: Simple animations, memes, and small icons.
pros: Small file size for simple graphics
